articles.title: Critical bug in CrowdStrike LogScale let attackers access files
articles.summary: CrowdStrike has patched a critical path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2026-40050) in its self-hosted LogScale product that could allow unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files from the server. Security updates have been released to address the flaw.

articles.title: American utility firm Itron discloses breach of internal IT network
articles.summary: American utility company Itron, Inc. has reported a cybersecurity breach involving unauthorized access to its internal IT network via an SEC 8-K filing. The company is currently investigating the incident to determine the scope of the impact.

articles.title: GopherWhisper: new China-linked APT targets Mongolia with Go-based malware
articles.summary: A China-linked APT group identified as GopherWhisper is targeting Mongolian government institutions using a sophisticated suite of Go-based loaders and backdoors. ESET researchers discovered this campaign, highlighting the group's focus on regional espionage.

articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 94
articles.summary: This newsletter highlights recent malware threats, including the Morpheus spyware, DarkSword and Coruna exploits targeting iPhones, and the Lotus Wiper targeting energy infrastructure. It provides a curated overview of critical cybersecurity research and emerging malicious activity.

articles.title: Trigona ransomware adopts custom tool to steal data and evade detection
articles.summary: Trigona ransomware has transitioned to a custom-built data exfiltration tool to improve efficiency and bypass security detection mechanisms previously triggered by standard utilities like Rclone. This shift reflects an evolving tactical approach aimed at gaining greater control over stolen data and evading discovery.

articles.title: Hot take: AI's not going to kill open source code security
articles.summary: The article argues against the prevailing sentiment that artificial intelligence poses an existential threat to the security of open-source software. It suggests that AI will likely serve as a tool to enhance rather than compromise secure development practices.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 574 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: The Security Affairs newsletter highlights CISA's addition of critical vulnerabilities in SimpleHelp, Samsung, and D-Link products to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

articles.title: Week in review: Claude Mythos finds 271 Firefox flaws, Vercel breach
articles.summary: This weekly review covers the discovery of 271 Firefox vulnerabilities using Claude Mythos, a Vercel security breach, the release of the SmokedMeat CI/CD security tool, and the emergence of NGate NFC malware targeting Android devices.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds SimpleHelp, Samsung, and D-Link flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include critical security flaws found in SimpleHelp, Samsung, and D-Link products. Federal agencies are required to address these vulnerabilities by specified deadlines to mitigate active exploitation risks.

articles.title: Microsoft rolls out revamped Windows Insider Program
articles.summary: Microsoft is introducing a revamped Windows Insider Program designed to address ongoing performance and reliability issues within Windows 11. This update aims to improve the overall quality of the operating system by refining the feedback and testing process.

articles.title: Threat actor uses Microsoft Teams to deploy new “Snow” malware
articles.summary: A threat actor identified as UNC6692 is utilizing social engineering via Microsoft Teams to distribute a new malware suite called 'Snow'. This custom malware includes a backdoor, a tunneler, and a browser extension.

articles.title: Over 400,000 sites at risk as hackers exploit Breeze Cache plugin flaw (CVE-2026-3844)
articles.summary: A critical, unauthenticated file upload vulnerability (CVE-2026-3844) in the Breeze Cache WordPress plugin is currently being exploited in the wild, putting over 400,000 websites at risk. The flaw carries a CVSS score of 9.8, allowing attackers to compromise servers without requiring login credentials.

articles.title: Fake CAPTCHA Scam Abuses Verification Clicks to Send Costly International Texts
articles.summary: Researchers have uncovered a widespread Click2SMS fraud campaign that uses deceptive CAPTCHA prompts and browser hijacking to trick users into sending unauthorized, premium-rate international text messages. The scheme exploits user interaction to generate fraudulent charges without victim consent.

articles.title: CISA reports persistent FIRESTARTER backdoor on Cisco ASA device in federal network
articles.summary: CISA discovered the persistent FIRESTARTER backdoor on a U.S. federal agency's Cisco Firepower ASA device, noting that the malware remained active even after the application of security patches.

articles.title: ADT confirms data breach after ShinyHunters leak threat
articles.summary: Home security company ADT has officially confirmed a data breach following extortion demands from the ShinyHunters hacking group. The group threatened to release stolen sensitive information unless their ransom demands were met.

articles.title: The npm Threat Landscape: Attack Surface and Mitigations
articles.summary: Unit 42 provides a comprehensive analysis of the evolving npm supply chain threat landscape, highlighting sophisticated attack vectors such as wormable malware and CI/CD persistence. The report outlines current attack surfaces and recommends strategies for mitigating software supply chain risks.

articles.title: Latest spy power reauthorization bill leaves critics unimpressed
articles.summary: Proposed legislation to reauthorize Section 702 surveillance powers is facing significant bipartisan opposition ahead of the upcoming April 30 deadline. The bill's outcome remains uncertain as critics from across the political spectrum raise concerns regarding the extension of these government spy powers.

articles.title: Firestarter malware survives Cisco firewall updates, security patches
articles.summary: Cisco ASA and FTD firewall devices are being targeted by persistent Firestarter malware that survives system updates and security patches. Cybersecurity agencies in the U.S. and U.K. have issued warnings regarding this sophisticated threat.

articles.title: TGR-STA-1030: New Activity in Central and South America
articles.summary: Unit 42 reports that the threat actor TGR-STA-1030 continues to show active malicious operations targeting entities in Central and South America.

articles.title: Windows Update gets new controls to reduce forced restarts
articles.summary: Microsoft is introducing updates to Windows to provide users with better control over installation schedules and minimize disruptive automatic restarts. These improvements aim to enhance the user experience by reducing the impact of forced update reboots.

articles.title: New ClickFix attack Hides in Native Windows Tools to Reduce Detection Risk
articles.summary: A new 'ClickFix' social engineering campaign utilizes fake CAPTCHA prompts to trick Windows users into executing malicious commands that leverage native tools for persistence and stealth. By using built-in utilities like cmdkey and regsvr32, attackers evade traditional security detections.

articles.title: 12-year-old Pack2TheRoot bug lets Linux users gain root privileges
articles.summary: A 12-year-old high-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-41651) in PackageKit, dubbed Pack2TheRoot, allows local unprivileged Linux users to gain unauthorized root access. The flaw permits users to install or remove system packages, posing a significant security risk.

articles.title: Iran’s cyber threat may be less ‘shock and awe’ than ‘low and slow,’ officials say
articles.summary: Experts indicate that Iranian cyber activity is shifting toward persistent, opportunistic intrusions rather than large-scale, disruptive attacks. This strategy aims to maximize the appearance of capability while maintaining a lower profile.

articles.title: ADT says customer data stolen in cyber intrusion
articles.summary: Home security company ADT confirmed that cybercriminals breached their systems, resulting in the theft of a limited amount of customer and prospective customer data.

articles.title: New BlackFile extortion group linked to surge of vishing attacks
articles.summary: A new threat actor called BlackFile is conducting data theft and extortion attacks against the retail and hospitality sectors using vishing techniques. The group has been active since February 2026.

articles.title: Microsoft to roll out Entra passkeys on Windows in late April
articles.summary: Microsoft is introducing phishing-resistant passkey support for Entra-protected resources on Windows devices starting in late April. This move aims to enhance security by enabling stronger passwordless authentication methods.

articles.title: New ‘Pack2TheRoot’ flaw gives hackers root Linux access
articles.summary: A vulnerability named Pack2TheRoot in the PackageKit daemon allows local Linux users to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges. This flaw enables unauthorized installation or removal of system packages, leading to a full system compromise.

articles.title: Pentagon grapples with securing AI as it moves toward autonomous warfare
articles.summary: The Pentagon is increasingly integrating autonomous weapons into its defense strategy while facing the significant challenge of securing these AI-driven systems. Gen. Dan Caine emphasized their necessity in modern warfare, highlighting the urgency for robust cybersecurity protocols.

articles.title: FIRESTARTER Backdoor Hit Federal Cisco Firepower Device, Survives Security Patches
articles.summary: CISA and the NCSC identified a new backdoor named FIRESTARTER that compromised a federal Cisco Firepower device. The malware persists despite security patches, enabling unauthorized remote access.

articles.title: US clarifies mobile hotspots part of foreign router ban despite rarity of American made consumer kit
articles.summary: The U.S. government has clarified that mobile hotspots are included under existing foreign router bans, even though domestically manufactured consumer networking equipment is currently uncommon. This policy adjustment aims to tighten restrictions on potentially compromised hardware within U.S. infrastructure.

articles.title: ShinyHunters claim they have cruise giant Carnival's booty as 7.5M emails surface
articles.summary: The hacking group ShinyHunters claims to have stolen data from Carnival Corporation, with approximately 7.5 million email addresses allegedly compromised. This incident represents a significant unauthorized data breach involving a major cruise operator.

articles.title: Governments on high alert after CISA snuffs out Firestarter backdoor on fed network
articles.summary: CISA has successfully neutralized the Firestarter backdoor found within a federal network, prompting widespread vigilance among government agencies. The discovery highlights an active effort to mitigate unauthorized access and potential long-term threats to critical infrastructure.

articles.title: Norway's prime minister proposes ban on social media access for young teens
articles.summary: The Norwegian government is proposing legislation to ban social media access for young teenagers, mandating that tech companies implement strict age verification tools. This initiative aims to increase corporate accountability regarding the online safety of minors.

articles.title: More ancient Linux device support faces the chop
articles.summary: The Linux kernel development team is planning to remove support for several older, legacy hardware architectures to streamline maintenance. This reflects a shift toward modernizing the codebase by deprecating outdated and rarely used device support.

articles.title: NASA Employees Duped in Chinese Phishing Scheme Targeting U.S. Defense Software
articles.summary: A Chinese national conducted a long-term spear-phishing campaign against NASA employees and other U.S. entities to illicitly acquire sensitive defense software and technical information. This operation bypassed export control laws by posing as a legitimate researcher to gain unauthorized access.

articles.title: DORA and operational resilience: Credential management as a financial risk control
articles.summary: The article details how DORA's Article 9 mandates strict authentication and access controls for EU financial institutions to bolster operational resilience. It highlights the regulatory requirements and the severe consequences of failing to implement these essential risk controls.

articles.title: TeamPCP Hijacks Bitwarden CLI, Uses Dependabot to Deploy Shai-Hulud Malware
articles.summary: The threat actor TeamPCP has compromised the Bitwarden CLI and leveraged GitHub Dependabot to distribute Shai-Hulud malware and tamper with AI-assisted coding tools.

articles.title: Signal phishing campaign targets Germany’s Bundestag President Julia Klöckner
articles.summary: Germany’s Bundestag President Julia Klöckner was targeted by a phishing campaign involving a fraudulent Signal group chat disguised as a CDU political group. This incident highlights the growing trend of utilizing encrypted messaging platforms as vectors for cyberattacks against high-profile political figures.

articles.title: Toronto police arrest three in Canada’s first mobile SMS blaster case
articles.summary: Toronto police have arrested three individuals for using a mobile SMS blaster to impersonate cellular towers for mass phishing and network disruption, marking the first case of its kind in Canada.

articles.title: Over 10,000 Zimbra servers vulnerable to ongoing XSS attacks
articles.summary: More than 10,000 publicly exposed Zimbra Collaboration Suite servers are currently being targeted by active exploitation of a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. Organizations are urged to patch their systems to prevent potential unauthorized access and data compromise.

articles.title: Users advised to drop passwords and make room for passkeys
articles.summary: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) has officially updated its guidance, recommending that users shift from passwords to passkeys to better defend against modern cyber threats. This shift marks a significant change in security standards, positioning passkeys as the primary authentication method for digital services.

articles.title: Intel bets the farm on AI inference to drag CPU back to the top table
articles.summary: Intel is strategically prioritizing AI inference capabilities in its next-generation processors to regain competitive dominance in the CPU market. This shift reflects a broader industry focus on integrating dedicated AI acceleration hardware directly into standard computing architecture.

articles.title: Indirect prompt injection is taking hold in the wild
articles.summary: Researchers from Google and Forcepoint have identified real-world evidence of indirect prompt injection attacks, where malicious instructions are hidden on web pages to hijack LLM-powered AI agents. This emerging threat leverages AI's ability to process external content to execute unauthorized commands.

articles.title: Bridging the AI Agent Authority Gap: Continuous Observability as the Decision Engine
articles.summary: The article explores the security risks of AI agents, arguing that the core issue lies in the governance of delegated authority rather than just the emergence of new autonomous actors. It proposes continuous observability as a necessary mechanism to manage and monitor these agentic workflows.

articles.title: 26 FakeWallet Apps Found on Apple App Store Targeting Crypto Seed Phrases
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers identified malicious apps on the Apple App Store that impersonate legitimate cryptocurrency wallets to steal users' seed phrases and private keys. The campaign, active since late 2025, uses deceptive browser redirects to distribute trojanized versions of popular wallet software.

articles.title: Microsoft beefs up Remote Desktop security with ... hard-to-read messages
articles.summary: Microsoft has updated Remote Desktop security protocols, though the implementation has drawn criticism for using confusing or difficult-to-read warning messages for users. This change aims to improve user awareness of security risks despite the reported usability issues.

articles.title: It's a myth that you need Mythos to find bugs: Open source models can do it just as well
articles.summary: Recent research suggests that open-source AI models are as effective as specialized proprietary models like Mythos for identifying software vulnerabilities. This challenges the notion that expensive, closed-source tools are required for automated bug hunting.

articles.title: Microsoft now lets admins uninstall Copilot on enterprise devices
articles.summary: Microsoft has introduced a new policy allowing enterprise IT administrators to uninstall the Copilot AI assistant from managed devices following the April 2026 Patch Tuesday updates. This provides organizations with greater control over the software environment on their corporate systems.

articles.title: French Police Arrest HexDex Hacker Over Mass Data Theft and Leaks
articles.summary: French authorities have arrested a 20-year-old individual linked to the HexDex hacking group for orchestrating large-scale data breaches against government entities, corporations, and sports organizations.

articles.title: Compromised everyday devices power Chinese cyber espionage operations
articles.summary: The NCSC and partner agencies have issued an advisory warning that China-linked threat actors are increasingly using botnets composed of compromised edge devices like routers for large-scale cyber espionage. Organizations are urged to monitor traffic from remote access and VPN connections to mitigate this threat.

articles.title: New Cisco firewall malware can only be killed by pulling the plug
articles.summary: State-sponsored attackers are utilizing a persistent backdoor named Firestarter to compromise Cisco security appliances. The malware is notable for its persistence, as it can only be removed by physically power-cycling the affected devices.

articles.summary: Bitwarden's CLI tool was compromised via a supply chain attack involving a malicious update to the @bitwarden/cli package, which contained harmful code embedded in bw1.js. The breach was facilitated by a compromised GitHub Action as part of a larger, ongoing campaign identified by Checkmarx.

articles.title: Tropic Trooper Uses Trojanized SumatraPDF and GitHub to Deploy AdaptixC2
articles.summary: The advanced persistent threat group Tropic Trooper is targeting Chinese-speaking users by distributing a trojanized version of SumatraPDF to deploy the AdaptixC2 agent and leverage VS Code tunnels for unauthorized remote access.

articles.title: Meta is overhauling how you sign in, manage settings, and protect your accounts
articles.summary: Meta is introducing a centralized account management system called 'Meta Account' to streamline sign-in, security, and settings across its various applications and devices. This transition will occur gradually over the next year, with users receiving notifications prior to the change.

articles.title: Greece relaxes Euro biometric border entry rules amid airport chaos
articles.summary: Greece has temporarily relaxed biometric entry requirements for the European Entry/Exit System (EES) to alleviate significant congestion and operational delays at its airports. This policy shift reflects the ongoing implementation challenges and administrative friction surrounding new EU-wide automated border control systems.

articles.title: UK gov pays public £550 to discuss Digital ID – then bans journalists from the room
articles.summary: The UK government has faced criticism for offering financial compensation to citizens to participate in discussions about digital ID while simultaneously excluding journalists from the event. This action has raised concerns regarding transparency and public policy oversight concerning sensitive personal identification systems.

articles.title: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS delivers memory-safe system tools and live patching for Arm servers
articles.summary: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, codenamed Resolute Raccoon, enhances OS security by integrating memory-safe Rust-based components and live patching for Arm servers. The release provides long-term security support through April 2031.

articles.title: LMDeploy CVE-2026-33626 Flaw Exploited Within 13 Hours of Disclosure
articles.summary: LMDeploy is facing active exploitation of a high-severity Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerability (CVE-2026-33626) occurring within 13 hours of its initial disclosure.

articles.title: OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 is out with expanded cybersecurity safeguards
articles.summary: OpenAI has released its latest model, GPT-5.5, which includes enhanced cybersecurity safeguards for enterprise and pro users. This update follows the recent launch of GPT-5.4 as part of the company's efforts to improve AI security.

articles.title: China-linked threat actors use consumer device botnets to evade detection, warn UK and partners
articles.summary: The UK's NCSC and international partners have issued a warning regarding China-linked threat actors who are leveraging large-scale botnets of compromised consumer hardware to disguise malicious traffic. These groups are hijacking devices such as routers and cameras to act as proxies, complicating detection efforts by security teams.

articles.title: Researchers find cyber-sabotage malware that may predate Stuxnet by five years
articles.summary: Security researchers have identified a piece of sophisticated cyber-sabotage malware that appears to predate the infamous Stuxnet worm by approximately five years. This discovery suggests that state-sponsored industrial espionage and sabotage operations were active much earlier than previously assumed.

articles.title: AI is speeding up nation-state cyber programs
articles.summary: Microsoft's Kaja Ciglic highlights that nation-state cyber programs are increasingly integrated with geopolitical power, with AI accelerating their capabilities. She advocates for more robust, multi-faceted international strategies beyond traditional sanctions to address state-sponsored threats and ransomware.

articles.title: A study of 1,000 Android apps finds a privacy policy logging gap
articles.summary: A study of 1,000 Android applications reveals a significant disconnect between developer logging practices and official privacy policies, leading to potential compliance failures with regulations like GDPR. This misalignment highlights that data collected for debugging often falls outside the scope of what is disclosed to users.

articles.title: Weak security means attackers could disable all of a city's public EV chargers
articles.summary: A security weakness in public electric vehicle charging infrastructure could allow malicious actors to remotely disable an entire city's charger network. This vulnerability highlights the risks inherent in the growing connectivity of smart urban infrastructure.

articles.title: Vercel attack fallout expands to more customers and third-party systems
articles.summary: Vercel has confirmed that its ongoing security breach has impacted a wider range of customers and third-party systems than previously identified. The expanding scope of the compromise creates significant downstream security risks for affected organizations.

articles.title: Dev targeted by sophisticated job scam: 'I let my guard down, and ran the freaking code'
articles.summary: A software developer was compromised after executing malicious code provided by threat actors posing as potential employers during a sophisticated job scam. This incident highlights the growing risk of social engineering attacks specifically targeting the developer community.

articles.title: Hackers exploit file upload bug in Breeze Cache WordPress plugin
articles.summary: Hackers are actively exploiting an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability within the Breeze Cache WordPress plugin. This flaw allows attackers to execute malicious code on affected servers.

articles.title: Frontier AI and the Future of Defense: Your Top Questions Answered
articles.summary: This article addresses the strategic implications of frontier AI for cybersecurity professionals and provides answers to common customer inquiries regarding its integration into defense operations. It acts as a guide for security leaders navigating the risks and opportunities presented by advanced AI technologies.

articles.title: US, UK agencies warn hackers were hiding on Cisco firewalls long after patches were applied
articles.summary: US and UK cybersecurity agencies revealed that attackers utilized persistent malware, dubbed Firestarter, to maintain access to Cisco firewalls even after security patches were deployed. The campaign, discovered on a federal agency's network, highlights the risk of post-exploitation persistence despite remediation efforts.

articles.title: US sanctions Cambodian senator for millions earned through scam compounds
articles.summary: The US Treasury Department has imposed sanctions on Cambodian senator Kok An and 28 associates for their involvement in operating large-scale scam centers. The action targets the illicit financial networks behind these fraudulent activities.

articles.title: Dragos: Despite AI use, new malware targeting water plants is ‘hype’
articles.summary: Security firm Dragos has labeled the ZionSiphon malware, allegedly designed to sabotage Israeli water systems, as ineffective amateur work driven by AI-hype. Experts conclude that the threat lacks the technical sophistication to pose a genuine risk to industrial control systems.

articles.title: Chinese attackers are pwning your infrastructure to use in attacks, 10 countries warn
articles.summary: Ten countries have issued a joint warning regarding Chinese state-sponsored actors compromising global infrastructure to facilitate further cyberattacks. This operation highlights a significant trend of threat actors weaponizing legitimate network devices to establish persistence.

articles.title: Bitwarden CLI npm package compromised to steal developer credentials
articles.summary: Attackers injected malicious code into the Bitwarden CLI npm package to steal developer credentials and distribute the payload to downstream projects. The compromise was quickly identified, but it highlights risks in software supply chain security.

articles.title: Surveillance campaigns use commercial surveillance tools to exploit long-known telecom vulnerabilities
articles.summary: Researchers have documented the first instance of mapping attack traffic to mobile signaling infrastructure, revealing that surveillance actors are leveraging long-standing telecommunications vulnerabilities via commercial tools.

articles.title: CISA: US agency breached through Cisco vulnerability, FIRESTARTER backdoor allowed access through March
articles.summary: CISA reported that an unnamed US government agency was compromised via a Cisco vulnerability, with attackers utilizing the FIRESTARTER backdoor to maintain persistent access through March. This incident highlights the risk of persistent unauthorized access following the initial exploitation of network vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Trigona ransomware attacks use custom exfiltration tool to steal data
articles.summary: Trigona ransomware operators have deployed a custom command-line utility designed to accelerate the exfiltration of sensitive data from victim networks. This update enhances their ability to conduct large-scale data theft more efficiently during cyberattacks.

articles.title: Surveillance companies exploiting telecom system to spy on targets’ locations, research shows
articles.summary: Research has revealed that surveillance companies are exploiting vulnerabilities in global telecom infrastructure to track individuals by impersonating legitimate cellular providers. This method allows for clandestine geolocation of targets without their knowledge.

articles.title: UNC6692 Impersonates IT Helpdesk via Microsoft Teams to Deploy SNOW Malware
articles.summary: The newly identified threat actor UNC6692 is using social engineering on Microsoft Teams to impersonate IT support staff and deploy custom malware. This campaign relies on deceptive tactics to compromise victim hosts by tricking users into accepting malicious chat invitations.

articles.title: Luxury cosmetics giant Rituals discloses data breach impacting member personal details
articles.summary: Luxury cosmetics company Rituals has confirmed a data breach in which unauthorized actors accessed and exfiltrated personal information, including names and addresses, from its My Rituals member database.

articles.title: Harvester APT Expands Spying Operations with New GoGra Linux Malware
articles.summary: The Harvester APT group has launched a new Linux malware strain dubbed GoGra, which uses deceptive PDFs and Microsoft APIs to conduct espionage in South Asia. This campaign highlights the group's evolving capabilities in covert command and control.

articles.title: Age checks could turn internet into an ID checkpoint, complains Proton CEO
articles.summary: Proton's CEO has criticized proposed age verification requirements, arguing that they could fundamentally transform the internet into a restrictive ID-based checkpoint system. The statement highlights concerns over user privacy and the potential for increased surveillance.

articles.title: A dozen allied agencies say China is building covert hacker networks out of everyday routers
articles.summary: A coalition of international intelligence agencies has issued a warning regarding a shift in tactics by Chinese-linked threat actors who are leveraging consumer-grade routers to establish clandestine cyberattack infrastructure. The report provides technical guidance for organizations to mitigate the risks associated with this persistent network compromise.

articles.title: New Checkmarx supply-chain breach affects KICS analysis tool
articles.summary: Checkmarx confirmed a supply-chain attack where malicious actors compromised their KICS analysis tool's Docker images and extensions to steal sensitive data from developer environments.

articles.title: China-linked hackers targeted Mongolian government using Slack, Discord for covert communications
articles.summary: The China-linked threat actor GopherWhisper has been identified targeting the Mongolian government using custom backdoors and legitimate platforms like Slack and Discord for command-and-control operations.

articles.title: Cosmetics giant Rituals discloses data breach affecting customers
articles.summary: Dutch cosmetics company Rituals has confirmed a data breach involving the unauthorized access and theft of customer information from its My Rituals membership database. The company is currently investigating the incident to determine the scope of the affected user data.

articles.title: Regular Password Resets Aren’t as Safe as You Think
articles.summary: Mandatory password resets are often counterproductive, as attackers frequently exploit helpdesk social engineering tactics to facilitate unauthorized account access. Organizations should prioritize more robust authentication methods over frequent reset requirements.

articles.title: iOS Flaw Let Deleted Notifications Linger, Apple Issues Fix
articles.summary: Apple released updates for iOS and iPadOS to address a notification logging flaw, CVE-2026-28950, which could allow unauthorized recovery of deleted messages. The vulnerability caused devices to retain notification data even after the user performed a deletion.

articles.title: Bitwarden CLI Compromised in Ongoing Checkmarx Supply Chain Campaign
articles.summary: The Bitwarden CLI package version 2026.4.0 was compromised through a malicious file, 'bw1.js,' as part of an ongoing supply chain attack identified by JFrog and Socket.

articles.title: Trump’s pick for CISA director withdraws from consideration
articles.summary: Sean Plankey has withdrawn his nomination for CISA director following concerns regarding his past service in the Coast Guard. The withdrawal follows opposition from Sen. Rick Scott, which had effectively stalled the confirmation process.

articles.title: House Republicans unveil data privacy law that would override state protections
articles.summary: House Republicans have introduced the SECURE Data Act, a proposed federal data privacy bill that would preempt and override existing state-level consumer privacy protections.

articles.title: American farms have a new steward for their safety net, disaster programs... Palantir
articles.summary: Palantir has been selected to manage and modernize the data systems supporting American agricultural disaster relief and safety net programs. This integration suggests a significant shift in how federal agencies utilize private data analytics firms to oversee national infrastructure and food security.

articles.title: Microsoft: Some Teams users can’t join meetings after Edge update
articles.summary: A recent Microsoft Edge browser update has caused a bug that prevents some Windows users from joining Microsoft Teams meetings. Microsoft has acknowledged the issue and is working on a resolution.

articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: $290M DeFi Hack, macOS LotL Abuse, ProxySmart SIM Farms +25 New Stories
articles.summary: The bulletin highlights recurring security failures in supply chains and persistent exploitation patterns, ranging from high-profile DeFi hacks to macOS Living-off-the-Land attacks. It emphasizes that attackers continue to succeed by targeting systemic vulnerabilities and unvetted software packages.

articles.title: Medical data of 500,000 Britons put up for sale on Chinese website
articles.summary: Sensitive medical and genetic data belonging to 500,000 UK citizens, held by the UK Biobank, has been offered for sale on a Chinese website. The compromised information includes blood samples, medical scans, and genetic sequences.

articles.title: IP Fabric MCP server adds governance and control to enterprise AIOps workflows
articles.summary: IP Fabric has launched a new Model Context Protocol (MCP) server designed to provide secure, governed integration between enterprise network operations data and AIOps workflows. The solution aims to address security and control limitations that typically hinder AI adoption in enterprise environments.

articles.title: Aqua Compass MCP server enables real-time investigation and containment of runtime threats
articles.summary: Aqua Security has launched Aqua Compass, an MCP server designed to facilitate automated, AI-driven investigation and remediation of runtime security threats in cloud-native applications. This tool allows security teams to actively contain risks rather than just identifying them.

articles.title: Medical data of 500k Biobank volunteers listed for sale on Alibaba, UK minister reveals
articles.summary: A UK government minister reported that the sensitive medical data of 500,000 Biobank volunteers has been illicitly listed for sale on the Alibaba platform. The incident highlights a significant breach involving the personal and health information of a large research participant group.

articles.title: UK warns of Chinese hackers using proxy networks to evade detection
articles.summary: The UK's NCSC and international partners have issued a warning regarding Chinese-nexus hackers leveraging vast networks of compromised consumer devices to mask malicious operations. This tactic allows threat actors to hide their origin, complicating attribution and detection efforts.

articles.title: Hybrid clouds have two attack surfaces and you’re not paying enough attention to either
articles.summary: This headline highlights that hybrid cloud environments introduce complex, dual attack surfaces that are frequently neglected by security teams. It warns that insufficient attention to both on-premises and cloud components leaves organizations vulnerable to exploitation.

articles.title: New GopherWhisper APT group abuses Outlook, Slack, Discord for comms
articles.summary: A state-sponsored threat actor dubbed GopherWhisper is targeting government entities using a custom Go-based toolkit and popular communication platforms like Outlook, Slack, and Discord for command and control. This campaign leverages legitimate services to evade detection while executing sophisticated espionage activities.

articles.title: [Webinar] Mythos Reality Check: Beating Automated Exploitation at AI Speed
articles.summary: This webinar discusses the escalating threat of AI-driven, automated exploitation, which significantly reduces the time available for security teams to patch vulnerabilities. It highlights the 'Collapsing Exploit Window' as a major risk factor for organizations.

articles.title: Google brings instant email verification to Android, no OTP needed
articles.summary: Google has launched cryptographically verified email credentials for Android via the Credential Manager API, allowing for secure, frictionless authentication without the need for OTPs. This implementation adheres to W3C standards to streamline user onboarding and enhance security.

articles.title: Project Glasswing Proved AI Can Find the Bugs. Who's Going to Fix Them?
articles.summary: Anthropic has restricted the release of its Project Glasswing AI model, which is highly capable of identifying software vulnerabilities, opting instead to collaborate with major tech companies to patch security flaws before they can be exploited. This move highlights the dual-use risks of advanced AI in cybersecurity.

articles.title: If cyber espionage via HDMI worries you, NCSC built a device to stop it
articles.summary: The UK's NCSC has developed a hardware device called SilentGlass to protect HDMI and DisplayPort connections from cyber espionage and potential exploitation. This plug-and-play solution aims to mitigate risks associated with monitors that can process and store sensitive data.

articles.title: Apple fixes iPhone bug that let FBI retrieve deleted Signal messages(CVE-2026-28950)
articles.summary: Apple released a security patch for CVE-2026-28950, a vulnerability in Notification Services that caused iPhones to retain deleted message notifications, which was previously exploited by the FBI. This fix ensures that messages intended for deletion are properly removed from the device's logging system.

articles.title: CISA orders feds to patch BlueHammer flaw exploited as zero-day
articles.summary: CISA has issued an emergency directive requiring U.S. federal agencies to patch a Microsoft Defender privilege escalation vulnerability known as BlueHammer that is actively being exploited as a zero-day.

articles.title: If malware via monitor cables is a matter of national security, this might be the gadget for you
articles.summary: The headline discusses a specialized hardware security tool designed to mitigate risks posed by malicious monitor cables capable of exfiltrating data. It highlights an emerging physical-layer attack vector that can potentially compromise sensitive information.

articles.summary: Researchers have identified a novel indirect prompt injection technique that leverages hidden website instructions to compromise AI assistants like GitHub Copilot. This vulnerability allows attackers to manipulate AI outputs by embedding malicious commands within accessible web content.

articles.summary: Leaked data from the RAMP dark web forum exposes the sophisticated, highly organized structure of the Russian ransomware marketplace involving thousands of users and vast amounts of operational data. This revelation provides a deep look into the professional roles, including brokers and recruiters, that facilitate global ransomware operations.

articles.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-33825, a Microsoft Defender vulnerability with a CVSS score of 7.8, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. This action mandates that federal agencies address the security flaw due to evidence of active exploitation.

articles.summary: A previously unknown China-aligned threat actor dubbed GopherWhisper has compromised 12 Mongolian government systems using a variety of Go-based backdoors and custom injectors. The campaign, discovered by ESET, highlights the group's sophisticated capability to deploy and execute persistent malware.

articles.summary: The newly identified China-aligned APT group GopherWhisper is utilizing legitimate collaboration platforms like Slack, Discord, Outlook, and file.io to mask command-and-control traffic. The group was recently linked to a cyber espionage operation targeting a Mongolian governmental entity.

articles.title: OpenAI tackles a bad habit people have when interacting with AI
articles.summary: OpenAI has released an open-source Privacy Filter model designed to automatically detect and redact personally identifiable information from text inputs. This tool aims to mitigate the security risks associated with users inadvertently sharing sensitive data with AI systems.

articles.title: Vercel Finds More Compromised Accounts in Context.ai-Linked Breach
articles.summary: Vercel has discovered more compromised customer accounts linked to a previous security breach after expanding its investigation and internal system review.

articles.title: Apple Patches iOS Flaw That Stored Deleted Signal Notifications in FBI Forensic Case
articles.summary: Apple released a security patch for iOS and iPadOS to resolve a vulnerability that caused deleted Signal notifications to be incorrectly retained on devices. The fix improves data redaction to prevent sensitive notification logs from being stored after deletion.

articles.title: Pass the key, passwords have passed their sell-by date
articles.summary: The headline advocates for the transition away from traditional password-based authentication in favor of more secure alternatives like passkeys. It emphasizes that passwords are increasingly obsolete due to their vulnerability to modern cyber threats.

articles.summary: A new variant of the GoGra Linux malware leverages the Microsoft Graph API and Outlook to stealthily deliver payloads. The threat is attributed to the Harvester cyberespionage group.

articles.title: A year in, Zoom’s CISO reflects on balancing security and business
articles.summary: Zoom CISO Sandra McLeod reflects on her first year, focusing on the transition from reactive incident management to proactive business strategy and leadership.

articles.summary: LangWatch has introduced Scenario, an open-source framework designed to perform automated, multi-turn red-teaming exercises against AI-driven applications. This tool aims to improve security by simulating complex, adversarial attacks that exceed the capabilities of traditional single-prompt penetration testing.

articles.title: GDPR works, but only where someone enforces it
articles.summary: A study reveals that GDPR's effectiveness in reducing web tracking is primarily limited to jurisdictions where regulators actively enforce the law. The findings underscore the critical role of enforcement in ensuring actual compliance with privacy regulations.

articles.title: Ransomware, fraud, and lawsuits drive cyber insurance claims to new peaks

articles.summary: Recent analysis suggests that Mythos, an AI model developed by Anthropic for automated bug hunting, has failed to live up to its hype regarding security research capabilities.

articles.title: Apple fixes iOS bug that retained deleted notification data
articles.summary: Apple has issued out-of-band security updates for iOS and iPadOS to resolve a vulnerability that caused deleted notification data to persist on user devices. The fix addresses a privacy flaw within the Notification Services component.

articles.title: North Korean hackers siphon more than $12 million from crypto users in sprawling campaign

articles.summary: House Republicans have introduced a federal privacy bill modeled after existing state-level legislation in Virginia and Kentucky. However, the proposal faces potential challenges due to a lack of bipartisan support.

articles.summary: A new Mirai-based botnet campaign is actively exploiting a high-severity command-injection vulnerability, CVE-2025-29635, in end-of-life D-Link DIR-823X routers to compromise devices.

articles.title: Google’s Workspace Intelligence promises privacy while running on your data
articles.summary: Google has introduced Workspace Intelligence, an AI-powered system designed to analyze and organize content across Google Workspace apps while emphasizing data privacy and compliance. The feature aims to provide secure insights by leveraging the existing security infrastructure of the Workspace platform.

articles.summary: Hackers utilized a previously unknown wiper malware to conduct destructive attacks against Venezuela's energy and utilities sector. The incident appears specifically engineered to cause permanent system damage.

articles.summary: The Kyber ransomware group is targeting Windows and VMware ESXi systems with a new variant that incorporates Kyber1024 post-quantum encryption algorithms. This development signals an early adoption of quantum-resistant cryptographic primitives by malicious actors to secure their extortion payloads.

articles.summary: Decentralized social media platforms Mastodon and Bluesky have both experienced significant service disruptions due to consecutive DDoS attacks. While the outages were impactful, they were resolved by the respective platforms within a few hours.

articles.title: Discord-Linked Group Accessed Anthropic’s Claude Mythos AI in Vendor Breach
articles.summary: Anthropic is investigating a security breach where a Discord-linked group gained unauthorized access to its Claude Mythos AI model via a third-party vendor. The company reports no evidence of impact on its core systems.

articles.title: Malicious KICS Docker Images and VS Code Extensions Hit Checkmarx Supply Chain
articles.summary: Threat actors compromised the official Checkmarx KICS Docker Hub repository by overwriting existing tags and injecting a malicious version, alongside reports of compromised VS Code extensions. This supply chain attack highlights significant risks to developers utilizing poisoned container images.

articles.summary: Researchers have discovered a self-propagating supply chain worm, dubbed CanisterSprawl, that compromises npm packages to hijack developer tokens for data exfiltration. The malware utilizes ICP canisters to securely manage stolen credentials while spreading across the ecosystem.

articles.title: Mirai Botnet exploits CVE-2025-29635 to target legacy D-Link routers
articles.summary: The Mirai botnet is actively exploiting a command injection vulnerability (CVE-2025-29635) in legacy D-Link routers following the release of a public proof-of-concept. The flaw allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands by sending crafted POST requests to the vulnerable devices.

articles.summary: The French government agency France Titres (ANTS) has reported a data breach impacting its online portal, which manages sensitive identity documents. The agency has issued a phishing alert as a security precaution following the incident.

articles.summary: This article provides a comparative analysis of Test Data Management (TDM) solutions from K2view and Broadcom to help organizations evaluate their architecture, integration, and security capabilities.

articles.title: The Supreme Court is about to decide how far geofence warrants can go
articles.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court is set to review the legality of geofence warrants in the Chatrie v. United States case, specifically addressing whether dragnet location data collection violates Fourth Amendment standards for probable cause.

articles.summary: French authorities have arrested a suspected hacker responsible for numerous data breaches targeting public and private institutions across France.

articles.summary: The threat actor Harvester is deploying a new Linux variant of the GoGra backdoor, utilizing the Microsoft Graph API and Outlook mailboxes as a covert command-and-control channel to evade network defenses. The campaign primarily targets entities in South Asia.

articles.summary: Dutch intelligence officials have warned that China's cyber capabilities are now on par with the United States, noting that Beijing's sophisticated operations frequently evade detection by global defense agencies. The report highlights an urgent need to address this growing, largely unmet threat to international cybersecurity.

articles.summary: Two new Mirai-based botnet variants, 'tuxnokill' and 'Nexcorium', have been discovered targeting routers and DVRs via newly identified vulnerabilities. The tuxnokill variant specifically exploits CVE-2025-29635 to propagate through IoT devices.

articles.summary: Elastic has introduced MCP Apps, enabling security and observability workflows directly within AI tools to streamline threat investigation and system diagnostics. articles.title: UK cyber agency handling four major incidents a week as nation-state attacks surge
articles.summary: The UK's cybersecurity agency is managing four major nation-state cyber incidents weekly, marking a shift from criminal-led attacks to state-sponsored threats.

articles.summary: Bluesky experienced a 24-hour service disruption following a DDoS attack claimed by the Iran-linked 313 Team. The company confirmed that no user data was compromised during the incident.

articles.summary: Recent market analysis indicates that corporate IT spending remains resilient despite global geopolitical instability and potential energy sector shocks. articles.summary: Microsoft has issued emergency out-of-band security updates to address a critical privilege escalation vulnerability affecting ASP.NET Core. Users are urged to apply these patches immediately to mitigate potential security risks.

articles.summary: The Mustang Panda threat group has launched a new campaign using a LOTUSLITE malware variant to target banking sectors in India and policy organizations in South Korea. articles.summary: More than 1,300 internet-exposed Microsoft SharePoint servers remain unpatched and vulnerable to ongoing exploitation of a known spoofing zero-day vulnerability.

articles.summary: A fuzzer named Mythos identified 271 potential vulnerabilities in Firefox, though security researchers noted that these flaws were simple enough to be discovered through manual inspection. This highlights the effectiveness of automated tools in finding low-hanging fruit in complex browser codebases.

articles.summary: A previously unknown data-wiping malware called Lotus was utilized in targeted cyberattacks against energy and utility companies in Venezuela. The discovery highlights a new threat specifically impacting critical infrastructure sectors.

articles.summary: Check Point researchers identified over 1,570 victims of The Gentlemen ransomware operation after analyzing a command-and-control server hosting the SystemBC proxy malware.

articles.summary: Oracle released VirtualBox 7.2.8 to address various stability issues, including a specific Guru Meditation error, and to add support for Linux kernel 7.0. The update includes patches for networking, graphics, and UEFI components across Linux and Windows guest environments.

articles.title: More Cisco SD-WAN bugs battered in attacks
articles.summary: Cisco SD-WAN vulnerabilities are currently being exploited by threat actors in active attacks. Organizations are urged to review security advisories and apply patches to mitigate risks.

articles.title: UK regulator to probe Telegram, teen chat sites for potential child safety violations

articles.summary: The 'ClickFix' campaign targets macOS users by leveraging deceptive pop-ups to trick victims into executing malicious AppleScript payloads designed to steal credentials and cryptocurrency wallets. articles.summary: The U.S. National Security Agency has reportedly adopted Anthropic’s Claude Mythos model for operations, prompting scrutiny regarding supply chain security and the balance between AI utility and risk. This development highlights ongoing tensions within the Department of Defense over the integration of private AI technologies in sensitive environments.

articles.title: Google Patches Antigravity IDE Flaw Enabling Prompt Injection Code Execution
articles.summary: Google patched a vulnerability in its Antigravity IDE that allowed attackers to achieve remote code execution by combining file-creation capabilities with insufficient input sanitization in the file-searching tool. This flaw enabled attackers to bypass security restrictions through malicious prompt injection.

articles.title: Former ransomware negotiator pleads guilty to BlackCat attacks
articles.summary: A former cybersecurity professional, Angelo Martino, has pleaded guilty to participating in BlackCat ransomware attacks against U.S. companies in 2023. The case highlights an insider threat incident where a negotiator exploited their expertise to facilitate criminal activity.

articles.title: Mythos can find the vulnerability. It can’t tell you what to do about it.
articles.summary: Anthropic's new AI model, Mythos, efficiently identifies security vulnerabilities but lacks the capability to provide remediation guidance. The report highlights that finding flaws remains significantly easier than executing the necessary follow-up fixes.

articles.title: Grinex crypto exchange shuts down, blames Western agencies for $13.7M breach
articles.summary: The Grinex cryptocurrency exchange has ceased operations following a $13.7 million security breach, while forensic analysis suggests the event may be an exit scam linked to sanctions evasion.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Cisco Catalyst, Kentico Xperience, PaperCut NG/MF, Synacor ZCS, Quest KACE SMA, and JetBrains TeamCity flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has expanded its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to include multiple critical flaws affecting software from Cisco, Kentico, PaperCut, Synacor, Quest, and JetBrains. Federal agencies are now required to remediate these specific vulnerabilities to mitigate the risk of active exploitation.

articles.title: NGate Android malware uses HandyPay NFC app to steal card data
articles.summary: A new variant of the NGate malware is targeting Android users by masquerading as a trojanized version of the HandyPay app to intercept and steal NFC payment information. This attack leverages malicious software to exfiltrate sensitive financial data from victim devices.

articles.title: Adaptavist Group breach spawns imposter emails as ransomware crew claims mega-haul
articles.summary: The Adaptavist Group has suffered a data breach, resulting in threat actors using stolen information to send imposter emails while a ransomware group claims to have exfiltrated a significant amount of data. This incident highlights a double-extortion approach combining system compromise with phishing campaigns.

articles.title: Bluesky hit by 24-hour DDoS attack as pro-Iran group claims responsibility
articles.summary: Bluesky experienced a 24-hour service outage caused by a sophisticated DDoS attack claimed by a pro-Iran hacker group. The incident disrupted the microblogging platform's operations throughout mid-April.

articles.title: Panasonic creates device-locked QR codes to speed facial biometric capture
articles.summary: Panasonic has developed QR codes locked to specific devices to streamline and secure the process of facial biometric data capture. This innovation aims to enhance identity verification efficiency while reducing risks associated with unauthorized code duplication.

articles.title: CISA Adds 8 Exploited Flaws to KEV, Sets April-May 2026 Federal Deadlines
articles.summary: CISA has added eight actively exploited vulnerabilities, including three in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager and one in PaperCut, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Federal agencies are required to remediate these flaws by established deadlines in April and May 2026.

articles.title: Iran claims US used backdoors to knock out networking equipment during war
articles.summary: Iran has alleged that the United States utilized intentional backdoors to disable its networking infrastructure during military conflicts. This claim highlights ongoing geopolitical tensions centered around potential state-sponsored cyber warfare capabilities.

articles.title: Researchers build an encrypted routing layer for private AI inference
articles.summary: Researchers have developed an encrypted routing layer using Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC) to enable AI model inference while keeping input data private. This technique allows distributed servers to compute results without exposing sensitive raw information.

articles.title: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: April 21, 2026
articles.summary: This post provides a curated list of active cybersecurity employment opportunities, highlighting a specific role for an Application Security Engineer in the Philippines.

articles.title: Vibe coding upstart Lovable denies data leak, cites 'intentional behavior,' then throws HackerOne under the bus
articles.summary: AI development platform Lovable denied a data breach following user reports of exposed credentials, attributing the issue to intentional user behavior while shifting blame to the HackerOne platform. The incident highlights communication friction between vendors and security researchers regarding vulnerability disclosure processes.

articles.title: Ukraine busts ‘bot farm’ supplying thousands of fake Telegram accounts to Russian spies
articles.summary: Ukrainian law enforcement dismantled a bot farm that provided thousands of fake Telegram accounts to Russian intelligence for disinformation campaigns. This operation disrupted a key infrastructure used for targeted influence operations against the country.

articles.title: KelpDAO suffers $290 million heist tied to Lazarus hackers
articles.summary: The DeFi protocol KelpDAO suffered a $290 million crypto-heist attributed to state-sponsored North Korean hackers known as the Lazarus Group. This incident highlights ongoing security risks within decentralized finance platforms targeting large-scale digital asset theft.

articles.title: China's Apple App Store infiltrated by crypto-stealing wallet apps
articles.summary: Malicious actors have uploaded 26 fraudulent cryptocurrency wallet apps to Apple's China App Store, designed to impersonate legitimate services and steal users' seed phrases to drain funds. This campaign highlights a significant security risk for iOS users targeting digital asset theft.

articles.title: Vercel Breach Linked to Context.ai, ShinyHunters Says It’s Not Involved
articles.summary: Vercel has confirmed a data breach originating from a third-party incident at Context.ai, with a threat actor offering allegedly stolen data for $2 million. The hacking group ShinyHunters has denied any involvement, claiming that other actors are using their name.

articles.title: Vuln in Google’s Antigravity AI agent manager could escape sandbox, give attackers remote code execution
articles.summary: A vulnerability in Google's Antigravity AI agent manager allows attackers to bypass sandbox protections via prompt injection, potentially leading to remote code execution. Despite security measures like throttled network access, the system remains susceptible to this exploit.

articles.title: The FTC’s AI portfolio is about to get bigger
articles.summary: The FTC is expanding its AI regulatory efforts to combat the rise of sexual deepfakes and AI-driven voice clone scams. This initiative signals a growing focus on enforcing new legal standards to prevent AI-enabled fraud and abuse.

articles.title: France’s ANTS ID System website hit by cyberattack, possible data breach
articles.summary: The French ANTS website, which processes sensitive government identification applications, suffered a cyberattack that may have resulted in a breach of personal user data. Authorities identified the incident on April 15 and are currently investigating the exposure.

articles.title: Vercel’s security breach started with malware disguised as Roblox cheats
articles.summary: Vercel suffered a security breach triggered by malware hidden in Roblox cheats, highlighting risks associated with interconnected SaaS applications and excessive permission privileges.

articles.title: The Gentlemen ransomware now uses SystemBC for bot-powered attacks
articles.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware gang has begun utilizing the SystemBC proxy malware to conduct bot-powered attacks, with researchers identifying a network of over 1,570 compromised corporate hosts. This integration indicates a shift toward more sophisticated, automated infrastructure for managing ransomware operations.

articles.title: Claude Desktop changes app access settings for browsers you don't even have installed yet
articles.summary: The Claude Desktop application has been found to pre-configure browser integration settings for web browsers that are not currently installed on the user's system. This behavior has raised privacy and security concerns regarding how the application manages permissions and browser-based access.

articles.title: Seiko USA website defaced as hacker claims customer data theft
articles.summary: Seiko USA's website was defaced by attackers who claim to have stolen the company's Shopify customer database and are demanding a ransom to prevent its release.

articles.title: Scattered Spider member Tyler Buchanan pleads guilty to major crypto theft
articles.summary: Tyler Buchanan, a member of the Scattered Spider threat group, has pleaded guilty in a US court to orchestrating a massive campaign of corporate hacking and cryptocurrency theft. The conviction follows his arrest by Spanish authorities for his role in targeting dozens of companies.

articles.title: Scot becomes second Scattered Spider-linked crook to plead guilty in US
articles.summary: A Scottish individual has pleaded guilty in a U.S. court for their involvement in the Scattered Spider cybercrime group, which is known for high-profile social engineering and ransomware attacks. This marks the second successful prosecution of an affiliate linked to the prolific threat actor.

articles.title: SGLang CVE-2026-5760 (CVSS 9.8) Enables RCE via Malicious GGUF Model Files
articles.summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-5760) in SGLang allows attackers to execute arbitrary code by supplying malicious GGUF model files. The flaw has been assigned a CVSS score of 9.8.

articles.title: Italian regulator fines national postal service orgs $15 million for data privacy violations
articles.summary: The Italian data protection regulator has issued fines totaling $15 million to Poste Italiane SpA and its subsidiary Postepay SpA for the unauthorized processing of personal data belonging to millions of users.

articles.title: Crypto infrastructure company blames $290 million theft on North Korean hackers
articles.summary: A cryptocurrency infrastructure company has attributed a $290 million theft to North Korean hackers, marking a significant incident affecting multiple platforms. The event highlights ongoing security challenges within the crypto industry.

articles.title: Fake TikTok Downloaders on Chrome and Edge Spying on 130,000 Users
articles.summary: Malicious browser extensions masquerading as TikTok downloaders on Chrome and Edge have compromised over 130,000 users. These extensions use device fingerprinting to spy on victims and exfiltrate sensitive browser data.

articles.title: Microsoft: Teams increasingly abused in helpdesk impersonation attacks
articles.summary: Microsoft has reported a rise in cyberattacks where threat actors impersonate helpdesk personnel via Microsoft Teams to compromise enterprise networks. The attackers exploit legitimate collaboration tools and external access vectors to facilitate lateral movement within compromised systems.

articles.title: Vercel breached via compromised third-party AI tool
articles.summary: Vercel suffered a security breach after attackers compromised a third-party AI tool, Context.ai, which provided access to a Vercel employee's credentials. This allowed unauthorized entry into internal systems and exposed a limited subset of customer data.

articles.title: Elon Musk fails to appear for questioning by French police over sexualized AI images on X
articles.summary: Elon Musk and CEO Linda Yaccarino failed to attend voluntary police interviews in Paris regarding the circulation of non-consensual sexualized AI imagery on the X platform.

articles.title: How to Remove Objects from Video: AI Tools & Pro Tips (2026)
articles.summary: The headline describes a guide for using AI tools to edit and remove objects from video footage. It does not relate to cybersecurity threats, vulnerabilities, or data protection.

articles.title: Cyberattack at French identity document agency may have exposed personal data
articles.summary: A cyberattack on a French government portal for identity documents and driver's licenses has potentially compromised users' personal information. The Interior Ministry is currently investigating the scope of the data exposure.

articles.title: The backup myth that is putting businesses at risk
articles.summary: The article warns that relying solely on data backups is insufficient for maintaining business continuity during downtime, arguing that Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BCDR) solutions are necessary to survive ransomware and outages.

articles.title: Bluesky blames app outage on ‘sophisticated’ DDoS attack
articles.summary: Bluesky experienced intermittent service disruptions due to a sophisticated distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack that began on April 15. The decentralized platform addressed the incident after receiving user reports regarding app availability.

articles.title: CVE-2023-33538 under attack for a year, but exploitation still unsuccessful
articles.summary: Hackers have been attempting to exploit the high-severity CVE-2023-33538 vulnerability in outdated TP-Link routers for over a year, though no successful compromises have been reported to date.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Vercel Hack, Push Fraud, QEMU Abused, New Android RATs Emerge & More
articles.summary: This week's cybersecurity landscape highlights a trend of attackers exploiting trusted channels, such as supply chain compromises and malicious software updates, to bypass security measures. The recurring pattern emphasizes a shift toward subverting trust rather than purely breaking system defenses.

articles.title: British Scattered Spider hacker pleads guilty to crypto theft charges
articles.summary: A British leader of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group has pleaded guilty in the U.S. to charges of wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. The case highlights ongoing legal efforts to prosecute members of the prolific threat actor collective.

articles.title: Why the Axios attack proves AI is mandatory for supply chain security
articles.summary: A suspected North Korean threat actor injected malicious code into the widely used Axios JavaScript library, exposing millions of users to supply chain risks. The incident highlights the urgent need for AI-driven security to detect and respond to such rapid, large-scale attacks.

articles.title: Microsoft releases Windows Server update fix to fix its April update fixes
articles.summary: Microsoft has issued a follow-up update for Windows Server to address issues introduced by its initial April patch. This highlights the ongoing challenges of ensuring patch stability while maintaining security.

articles.title: British Hacker Tyler Buchanan Pleads Guilty to $8M Hacking Scheme in US
articles.summary: British national Tyler Buchanan has pleaded guilty to orchestrating an $8 million cryptocurrency theft scheme linked to the Scattered Spider threat group. The case marks a significant legal outcome for U.S. authorities targeting international cybercriminal activity.

articles.title: Microsoft tests Windows Explorer speed, performance improvements
articles.summary: Microsoft is testing performance enhancements and launch speed optimizations for Windows 11 File Explorer within the Insider program. These updates focus on system usability rather than security patching.

articles.title: British hacker tied to Scattered Spider campaign pleads guilty in $8M scheme
articles.summary: A British hacker has pleaded guilty in U.S. federal court to involvement in an $8 million cryptocurrency theft scheme linked to the notorious Scattered Spider hacking group. The perpetrator engaged in a large-scale cybercrime operation targeting both corporate and individual victims.
